Ajay Prakash Upadhyay vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home
Lko. on 21 February, 2023

Author: Rajeev Singh
Bench: Rajeev Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
?Court No. - 16
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 4267 of 2022
Applicant :- Ajay Prakash Upadhyay

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Suresh Kumar Upadhyay Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajeev Singh,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant inF.I.R. No. 40 of 2021, under Sections 409, 420, 120B IPC, Police Station Gomtinagar, District Lucknow with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is the employee of the company, which allegedly cheated the money, but merely on the basis of allegation that the applicant was associated with the Directors of the company, he has been falsely implicated in the present case as well as in other cases related to the offence committed by the company.
It is further submitted that the applicant does not have any criminal antecedent prior to the lodging of the F.I.R.s against the company, in which, the applicant has also been dragged.

It is also submitted that the charge sheet Ajay Prakash Upadhyay vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142298910/
1 has been filed and there is no possibility of tampering of any evidence.

entities.text: Ajay Prakash Upadhyay vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is lastly submitted that the applicant, who is in jail since 18.08.2021.
In such circumstances, applicant is entitled for bail.
It is also submitted that the applicant will never misuse the liberty of bail and shall fully cooperate in the investigation.
Learned A.G.A. opposes the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant and submits that the amount of more than Rs.5 crore of the investors was deposited in the company through the applicant.

It is further submitted that the applicant is also one of the kingpin, who motivated the people for depositing the money in the company However, learned A.G.A. does not dispute that the applicant is the employee of the company.

Considering the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. and going through the contents of F.I.R., bail application as well as other relevant documents, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Application stands allowed.

Let applicant -Ajay Prakash Upadhyay be released on bail in F.I.R. No. 40 of 2021, under Sections 409, 420, 120B IPC, Police Station Gomtinagar, District Lucknow, on his furnishing personal bond and two reliable sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(1) The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.

(2) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police office or tamper with the evidence.
(3) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(4) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A IPC.

(5) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A IPC.
